4 1.

This is a claim petition U/s 166 read with Section 140 ( Old )of The Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988,
filed by petitioners.

The brief facts of the case are that on 09.08.2014 at about 05:00 AM near Aasudham Society PS Chhawla the deceased Arun Kumar Yadav S/O Late Sh Kapleshwar Yadav was driving the truck bearing no. DL1GB6773 coming from Rewla side and proceedings towards Gurgaon, Haryana.

When the deceased reached towards near Aasudham Society, one tractor bearing No. HR10J5334 was coming from Gurgaon side and proceedings towards the Rewala side, collided with truck/ tanker bearing No. DL1GB6773, with such a forceful impact that the driver of the truck/tanker received grievous injuries.

The deceased was removed to RTRM Hospital,
Jaffarpur Kalan where his MLC No. 4290/14 was prepared.
The postmortem of deceased was also conducted vide PM No. 192/14.
The present claim application pertains to death of deceased Arun Kumar Yadav.
2. It is contended that said accident took place, due to use of offending vehicle by Jai Karan in negligent manner who has been impleaded as respondent no. 3.
The owner of the truck is Sh Meharban , who is impleaded as respondent no. 1.
And as the said vehicle/tractor was insured with Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd hence it is impleaded as respondent no. 2 in the present case.

By the present case, the petitioners are claiming a sum of Rs. 1,00,00,000/ (Rupees One crore Only) from respondents as compensation alongwith interest @ 12% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

3. Respondent No.1 has not filed any reply/ W.S.
4. Respondent no. 2 (insurance company) has filed its written statement and denied the involvement of offending vehicle/ tractor No. HR10J5334.
It is submitted that the accident had taken place due to negligence driving on the part of deceased himself while driving his truck.
The police has investigated the case and it has been found that deceased was driving the truck in rash and negligent manner and hit against the Tractor bearing No. HR10J5334.
The police has filed a closure report in this case stating therein that driver of offending truck had died and offence stands abetted.

5. Respondent No.3 has not filed any reply/ W.S.
6.

After completion of the proceedings, and subsequently made the driver as respondent No.3 the following issues were framed as under:
(i) Whether Arun Kumar Yadav S/o Late Kapleshwar Yadav sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 09.08.2014 caused due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle (Tractor)
no. HR10J5334 being driven by R.3 and owned by R1 and insured with R2 ?

OPP. 
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
(iii) Relief.

5 6.
In order to prove their claim, petitioners have examined petitioner no. 6 as PW1 (Smt. Anar Devi), mother of the deceased.
PW2. Sh. Sharvan Yadav as an eye witness and PW3 Ram Dai, wife of deceased.
No evidence was led by any of the respondents.
7. I have heard ld. counsels appearing on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.2.
and none appeared on behalf of respondent No.1 and 3.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission and I also perused the record.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE NO. 1:
Whether Arun Kumar Yadav S/o Late Kapleshwar Yadav sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 09.08.2014 caused due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle (Tractor) no. HR 10J5334 being driven by R3, owned by R1 and insured with R2 ? OPP.
8.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.

To prove this issue petitioners have examined PW2 Sarvan Kumar, as an eye witness who has deposed that on 09.08.2014, at about 5.00 A.M, the deceased was driving the truck/ tanker bearing no. DL1GB6773 and was coming from Rewla side and proceedings towards Gurgaon, Haryana.

He has deposed that when the deceased reached towards near Aasudham Society, one tractor bearing No. HR 10J5334 came from Gurgaon side towards Rewala side and collided with truck/ tanker bearing No. DL1GB6773, with such a forceful impact that the driver of the truck/tanker received Multiple injuries.
He has deposed that the accident took place due to sole negligence of the driver of tractor.
He has deposed that deceased was removed to RTRM Hospital, Jaffarpur Kalan where his MLC No. 4290/14 Ex PW1/1 was prepared.

The postmortem of deceased was also conducted vide PM No. 192/14 Ex PW1/2.
9.
Considered and perused the record.
The petitioners have filed the present claim application qua the death of Sh Arun Kumar Yadav being died in a motor vehicular accident dt 09.08.2014, within the jurisdiction of P.S Chhawla, Delhi.
They have examined PW2 Sh Sharvan Yadav, as an eye witness, who is also brother in law ( Sala) of the deceased.
PW2 has stated in affidavit Ex PW2/A that he is an eye witness in the accident occurred on 09.08.2014 and narrated the circumstances as to how accident was occurred.
But to come to the conclusion whether he was eye witness to the accident or not.
The cross examination of PW2 as well as charge sheet being filed alongwith the reply by Insurance company are to be analyzed minutely.
10. PW2 has deposed in his cross examination that be does not aware of the contents of his examination in chief being filed through affidavit Ex PW2/A.
He has deposed that he had never visited the P.S to get record his statement.
Volunteered he has stated that he was upset at that time.
Simultaneously, he has stated in his cross examination that he was working as Helper on the vehicle of the deceased and police has also met to him.
This witness has also deposed that he had told the police official present at the spot that he had seen the accident.
He has deposed that after the accident the deceased was got admitted by his brother.
But simultaneously, he has deposed that he has not filed any criminal complaint against the driver of alleged offending Tractor.
He has also admitted that he has not filed any complaint with the higher police authority or before the Ld MM where the cancellation report was filed by the police.
He has also deposed in his cross examination that he has not accompanied the deceased and he had not sustained any injury in the accident.

Smt. Ram Dai vs Meharban on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61723202/
6 11.
After analyzing the evidence on record the presence of PW2 is highly suspicious.
The MLC shows that the deceased was admitted in the hospital by the PCR and not by the brother of the deceased as deposed by PW2.

If the brother of the deceased could have admitted the deceased in the hospital than certainly name of the victim and name of the person who admitted the victim find mentioned on MLC which is not there.
Moreover PW2 has deposed in his cross examination that he had not accompanied the deceased to the hospital.
This version of PW2 also make his testimony highly suspicious regarding his presence at the time of accident in the truck being driven by the deceased.

If he was socalled helper on the truck of the deceased and was also the brother in law (Sala) of the deceased then he could have accompanied the deceased to the hospital and it is not the case of PW2 that he was unconscious at the time of accident.

12. On the other hand, the charge sheet has been field by the Investigating Officer, after investigation, in which statement of an eye witness Satpal Singh has been recorded who has categorically stated that it was the driver of the truck bearing No. DL 1G B6773 who was driving the truck in rash and negligent manner and hit the tractor which ( tractor) was broken in three pieces and driver of the tractor was thrown away from the tractor in the field.
And one person struck between mudguard and tyre.
The investigating officer categorically stated in the charge sheet that it was Arun Kumar Yadav, (the deceased) who has caused the accident by driving the truck in rash and negligent manner.

In a petition being filed U/S 166 of M V Act, though for arriving at a conclusion that the offending vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent is to be judged on the preponderance of probability and a touchstone of prima facie, has to be prevail.

But here in the present case, the evidence shows that PW2 was not present at the scene of crime and the investigating agency come to the conclusion that it was the victim who was diving his truck bearing No. DL 1GB6773 in rash and negligent manner.
A person cannot claim for his own wrong.
Reliance is placed on Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Meena Variyal 2007 (5) SCC 428 where Hon'ble Supreme Court has held:

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Meena Variyal 2007 (5) SCC 428
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Before we proceed to consider the main aspect arising for decision in this Appeal, we would like to make certain general observations.

It may be true that the Motor Vehicles Act, insofar as it relates to claims for compensation arising out of accidents,
is a beneficent piece of legislation.
It may also be true that subject to the rules made in that behalf, the Tribunal may follow a summary procedure in dealing with a claim.
That does not mean that a Tribunal approached with a claim for compensation under the Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
Ordinarily, a contract of insurance is a contract of indemnity.

When a car belonging to an owner is insured with the insurance company and it is being driven by a driver employed by the insured, when it meets with an accident, the primary liability under law for payment of compensation is that of the driver.
Once the driver is liable, the owner of the vehicle becomes vicariously liable for payment of compensation.
It is this vicarious liability of the owner that is indemnified by the insurance company.

A third party for whose benefit the insurance is taken, is therefore entitled to show, when he moves under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, that the driver was negligent in driving the vehicle resulting in the accident; that the owner was vicariously liable and that the insurance company was bound to Smt. Ram Dai vs Meharban on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61723202/
7 indemnify the owner and consequently, satisfy the award made.

Therefore, under general principles, one would expect the driver to be impleaded before an adjudication is claimed under Section 166 of the Act as to whether a claimant before the Tribunal is entitled to compensation for an accident that has occurred due to alleged negligence of the driver."

13. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd Vs Nirmala Devi & Ors in MAC. APP 20/2017 decided on 5 th July 2017 has also reiterated the obsevations of Hon'ble Supreme Court made in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Meena Variyal ( Supra).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the respondents and against petitioner by holding that victim Arun Kumar Yadav died in a motor vehicle accident due to his own rash and negligent driving of truck bearing No. DL 1GB 6773.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
15.
Since this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that deceased/victim was negligent in driving of truck bearing No. DL 1GB6773.
And a person who is main tortfeasor cannot claim for his own wrong.
So this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners are not entitled for any compensation from either of the respondents.
This issue is decided accordingly.
(RELIEF)
16. Petition stands dismissed.
